narrativeReportMd:
# DataRequirement R4-to-R6 breaking-change assessment

## Bottom line
`DataRequirement` keeps its canonical identity and most existing element shape, but it has material migration risk. The main hard break is the required `DataRequirement.type` binding moving from R4 `all-types` to R6 `fhir-types`, because some R4 type codes are no longer valid R6 type codes and R6 introduces new type codes that R4 cannot validate. R6 also adds `valueFilter`, which is not R4-representable in core.

## Scope
The analysis is local to `DataRequirement`. Base datatype hierarchy and inherited `Element`/`Extension` changes are out of scope and should be owned by base-artifact reports.

## Main migration themes
The existing element names, cardinalities, choice types, reference target for `subjectReference`, `codeFilter` and `dateFilter` constraints, and `sort.direction` code system remain stable. Migration risk comes from version-specific terminology and R6-only expressivity: type-code validation, participant subject terminology, and the new value-filter filter family.

## Highest-impact findings
1. `DataRequirement.type` required binding changed to the R6 type universe, creating both R4-to-R6 validation failures and R6-to-R4 representability gaps.
2. R6 `DataRequirement.valueFilter` can express constraints that have no R4 core element, causing lossy downgrade unless carried in an extension or rejected.
3. `subject[x]` uses a broader participant-resource ValueSet and a different terminology system, which is mostly conformance/runtime risk rather than a clear structural break.

## Findings requiring human review
Type-code migration and `valueFilter` downgrade need human or authoritative mapping review. A local StructureDefinition comparison identifies the issue but cannot determine clinical equivalence for every removed or replacement resource/type code.

## Backward-compatible design observations
The R6 additions are mostly additive for R4-to-R6 instances, but cross-version compatibility would have been easier with explicit ConceptMaps, legacy aliases, or standardized cross-version extensions for new filter content.

## Follow-up analysis
Review the `DataType` base-artifact report for the baseDefinition shift and obtain official type/resource ConceptMaps and terminology expansions before automating large-scale migration.

summary.executiveSummaryMd: `DataRequirement` has one high-impact hard break in the required `type` binding and one high-impact R6-to-R4 round-trip gap from the new `valueFilter`. The main uncertainty is not whether the computable differences exist, but how each changed type code should map semantically across versions.
summary.migrationThemesMd: Migration should focus on three areas: validating and remapping `DataRequirement.type` codes against the R6 type universe; deciding how to preserve or reject R6 `valueFilter` content when downgrading; and updating subject terminology handling from R4 `subject-type`/`resource-types` coding to R6 `participant-resource-types`/`fhir-types` coding.
summary.confidenceSummaryMd: Confidence is high for structural and binding deltas because both StructureDefinitions and relevant local ValueSets/CodeSystems were inspected. Confidence is medium for exact terminology impact because no live expansion service, official diff, or authoritative R4-to-R6 type ConceptMap was available.

findings.title: DataRequirement.type required binding changed from R4 all-types to R6 fhir-types

oldState.summary: Required code bound to R4 ValueSet/all-types|4.0.1.

binding.description: A list of all the concrete types defined in this version of the FHIR specification - Abstract Types, Data Types and Resource Types.

terminologyComparison.terminologyNotesMd: The local R4 `all-types` compose includes three systems: `data-types`, `resource-types`, and `abstract-types`. The R6 binding uses the unified `fhir-types` system. Comparing local CodeSystem concept trees showed numerous removed and added code strings; examples are shown here rather than embedding the full list.

oldState.narrativeMd: In R4, `DataRequirement.type` is mandatory and required-bound to `ValueSet/all-types|4.0.1`, composed from R4 data type, resource type, and abstract type code systems.

newState.summary: Required code bound to R6 ValueSet/fhir-types|6.0.0-ballot4.

binding.description: List of FHIR types (resources, data types).

terminologyComparison.terminologyNotesMd: R6 uses `ValueSet/fhir-types|6.0.0-ballot4`, backed locally by `CodeSystem/fhir-types`. The comparison was by local CodeSystem concept definitions, not by a terminology-server expansion.

newState.narrativeMd: In R6, `DataRequirement.type` remains mandatory but is required-bound to the R6 FHIR type universe. This changes which literal type codes are conformant.

facts.note: Binding strength did not change; the break comes from the required value set content changing.
Examples of R4 type code strings found in local R4 all-types concepts but not in local R6 fhir-types concepts.
Examples of R6 type code strings not present in the R4 all-types concept set.

structuredDelta.matchingRationaleMd: The element id and path are unchanged (`DataRequirement.type`), with identical cardinality and type. Only the required binding target and type code universe changed.

impact.impactRationaleMd: This is a direct conformance break for affected instances because `DataRequirement.type` is mandatory and has a `required` binding in both versions. An R4 instance with `type: "DeviceUseStatement"` or `type: "RequestGroup"` can be valid against R4 `all-types` but fail R6 required-binding validation. Conversely, R6 instances using new codes such as `RequestOrchestration` or `integer64` cannot validate as R4 `all-types` values. Generated enums and switch statements over FHIR type codes are also likely to need regeneration.
impact.safetyOrBusinessRiskMd: DataRequirement is commonly used in knowledge artifacts and decision-support logic. Incorrectly remapping or dropping type codes can change which data a module requests, with potential clinical or business-rule consequences.

justification.inferredGoal: Align DataRequirement.type with the R6 FHIR type universe and the unified R6 fhir-types terminology.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Retain mapped R4 type codes as deprecated aliases in the R6 base type value set while making canonical R6 fhir-types authoritative.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: The inferred R6 goal is reasonable: `DataRequirement.type` should identify requestable types in the R6 model, and FHIR's type/resource inventory changed across major versions. A less-breaking alias transition could reduce old-valid/new-invalid failures, but it would not fully meet the goal for all R4 values because some names refer to removed, renamed, or materially changed concepts. Allowing those codes in a required base R6 binding would weaken conformance clarity, so the breaking design is probably justified despite a partial alternative.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: The best base-design alternative would be to include selected R4 `all-types` code strings in the R6 `fhir-types` value set as deprecated legacy aliases, with canonical mappings where safe. That is more than migration tooling because it changes what base R6 validators accept. It is only a partial alternative: obsolete aliases could accumulate indefinitely, some R4 codes may not have one safe R6 meaning, and systems could continue dispatching on noncanonical names rather than normalizing to R6 types.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: Aliases would preserve some legacy instances, but they risk validating obsolete or ambiguous type names and still require review for renamed, removed, split, or semantically changed types.

evidence.detail: R4 binds DataRequirement.type with required strength to ValueSet/all-types|4.0.1.
R6 binds DataRequirement.type with required strength to ValueSet/fhir-types|6.0.0-ballot4.
R4 all-types composes data-types, resource-types, and abstract-types systems.
Local concept comparison found R4 type code examples absent from R6 and R6 type code examples absent from R4.

examples.examplesMd: The fragments are datatype-level examples. `DeviceUseStatement` is an R4 type code not present in the local R6 fhir-types CodeSystem. `RequestOrchestration` is an R6 type code not present in the R4 all-types concept set and is a plausible migration target for some, but not necessarily all, R4 `RequestGroup` usages.

findings.narrativeMd: `DataRequirement.type` still looks structurally unchanged, which makes this easy to miss: it is still a required `code` at the same path. The breaking change is in the required terminology. Systems that validate type codes, generate enums from ValueSets, or dispatch logic by DataRequirement type must update for the R6 type universe and cannot assume every R4 code remains valid.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: For R4-to-R6, any R4 DataRequirement whose `type` code was removed or renamed in the R6 type universe can become invalid under required-binding validation. For R6-to-R4, new R6 type codes cannot be represented as valid R4 `all-types` values. Runtime risks include failed validation, enum deserialization errors, unhandled switch cases, and incorrect data retrieval if a removed type is silently mapped to the wrong R6 type.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Regenerate FHIR type-code enums from R6 definitions and inventory DataRequirement instances for codes outside R6 `fhir-types`. Use an authoritative cross-version ConceptMap where available; otherwise treat mappings such as `RequestGroup` to `RequestOrchestration` as review-required, not automatic. Preserve `profile` values during migration and test both strict validation and runtime dispatch for old, renamed, removed, and new type codes.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: Because FHIR major versions legitimately change the available type universe, the required-binding change is probably justified. The compatibility gap could be reduced by a normative ConceptMap, deprecated aliases, or migration extensions, but keeping obsolete type codes in the base R6 required ValueSet would blur conformance and could make R6 artifacts appear to request data types that no longer exist.
findings.reviewerNotesMd: The local comparison did not use an official terminology expansion or change rationale. Before bulk migration, confirm exact mappings for each removed R4 type code using official cross-version materials.

freshReview.narrativeMd: R4 and R6 keep `DataRequirement.type` as a mandatory `code`, but the required binding moves from R4 `all-types` to R6 `fhir-types`. That is a real compatibility break for affected artifacts: an R4 data requirement with a removed or renamed type code such as `DeviceUseStatement`, `RequestGroup`, or `Any` can fail R6 required-binding validation and generated enum/switch logic until it is mapped. The break appears proportionate because the set of FHIR types legitimately changes across major versions, and accepting obsolete names in the base R6 type universe would make it look as if removed R4 types are still requestable R6 data.
keyEvidence: R4 StructureDefinition DataRequirement.type: min 1, max 1, type code, required binding to http://hl7.org/fhir/ValueSet/all-types|4.0.1.
R6 StructureDefinition DataRequirement.type: min 1, max 1, type code, required binding to http://hl7.org/fhir/ValueSet/fhir-types|6.0.0-ballot4.

Local terminology comparison: R4 all-types includes data-types, resource-types, and abstract-types; examples present in R4 and absent in R6 include DeviceUseStatement, RequestGroup, Any, MoneyQuantity, and SimpleQuantity; examples present in R6 and absent in R4 include RequestOrchestration, CodeableReference, integer64, CanonicalResource, and MetadataResource.

R4/R6 StructureDefinitions use DataRequirement in knowledge-artifact paths including Library.dataRequirement, PlanDefinition action inputs/outputs, GuidanceResponse.dataRequirement, and TriggerDefinition.data.
freshReview.fmmEffect: The supplied/local R4 maturity context is trial-use standards status with no numeric FMM found in the R4 maturity map. That softens the stability burden compared with normative/FMM 5 content, but the mandatory type code is central to DataRequirement dispatch in knowledge artifacts, so the break remains meaningful.
freshReview.compatibilityMechanism: old-valid/new-invalid: R4-valid DataRequirement.type codes outside the R6 fhir-types value set fail required-binding validation; runtime/API/codegen enum and switch handling may also need migration.
freshReview.lessBreakingAlternativeAssessment: A less-breaking R6 design could add deprecated legacy R4 type aliases to the R6 fhir-types value set, possibly with canonical mappings. That would preserve some old instances but is only a partial solution because some old codes are removed, renamed, or semantically ambiguous, and accepting them in a required R6 type value set would weaken conformance clarity.
freshReview.comparisonToExisting: partially agree with the existing high-impact assessment because affected strict validators and generated clients do break; I agree any less-breaking alternative is only partial and do not see this as disproportionate enough to revisit.

findings.title: R6 adds DataRequirement.valueFilter with no R4 core representation

oldState.summary: No valueFilter element exists in R4 DataRequirement.
oldState.narrativeMd: R4 can express code-based filters through `codeFilter` and date/range filters through `dateFilter`, but it has no core `valueFilter` element or subelements.

newState.summary: R6 adds optional repeating valueFilter with path, searchParam, comparator, and value[x].
newState.narrativeMd: R6 `valueFilter` is an optional repeating element. It has `path` and `searchParam` string subelements, an optional `comparator` code required-bound to `eq`, `gt`, `lt`, `ge`, `le`, `sa`, and `eb`, and `value[x]` choices of `dateTime`, `Period`, and `Duration`.

facts.note: Optional repeating Element added in R6.

structuredDelta.matchingRationaleMd: The R6 `valueFilter` element and children have no matching R4 element ids or paths. They are a new local element family, not a rename of `codeFilter` or `dateFilter` because those existing elements remain unchanged.

impact.impactRationaleMd: Adding an optional element does not make existing R4 DataRequirement instances invalid in R6. The high impact is in the reverse direction: an R6 artifact that relies on `valueFilter` cannot be losslessly represented using R4 core elements. R4 parsers or generated classes may also reject or drop the unknown element when receiving R6 content.
impact.safetyOrBusinessRiskMd: Dropping a filter from a knowledge artifact can broaden or otherwise alter the requested data set, which can change measure, CDS, or query behavior.

justification.inferredGoal: Allow DataRequirement to constrain values beyond the code-valued and date-valued filter families available in R4.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Not applicable: `valueFilter` is an optional R6 addition and does not make R4-valid DataRequirement instances invalid in R6.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: Adding an optional value-filter family is a reasonable R6 base design for representing constraints that R4 could not express natively. The reported compatibility issue is high for R6-to-R4 round-tripping, not for preserving R4 instances under R6 validation. Because no R4-to-R6 base break is introduced, a backward-compatible alternative is not applicable.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: A standardized R4 or cross-version extension could help carry `valueFilter` content when downgrading, but under the calibration rules that is a mitigation, not a less-breaking R6 base-design alternative. Keeping the concept only as an extension would improve cross-version round-trip symmetry but would make an R6-native query constraint less discoverable and less consistently validated.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: R6-to-R4 export still needs an extension, rejection, or loss policy, but that is a down-conversion mitigation rather than a less-breaking R6 base design.

evidence.detail: No R4 element id begins with DataRequirement.valueFilter.
R6 valueFilter.value[x] allows dateTime, Period, and Duration.
R6 valueFilter.comparator is required-bound to comparator codes eq, gt, lt, ge, le, sa, and eb.

examples.examplesMd: The example illustrates an R6 DataRequirement that depends on `valueFilter`. R4 has no equivalent core element, so a downgrade must either preserve this through an extension or lose the filter.

findings.narrativeMd: R6 adds a new filter family for value constraints. This is not a direct R4-to-R6 validation break because the element is optional, but it is a significant round-trip and runtime risk: R4 schemas/classes do not know about `valueFilter`, and silently dropping it changes the meaning of the DataRequirement.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: R4-valid instances without `valueFilter` remain valid with respect to this addition in R6. Valid R6 instances that contain `valueFilter` are not cleanly representable in R4 core. Strict R4 parsers will reject the unknown element; lenient parsers may drop it; generated R4 models will not expose a property for it. All three behaviors can break migration or data-retrieval semantics.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: When downgrading R6 to R4, detect `DataRequirement.valueFilter` explicitly. If the content must be preserved, use an agreed extension or a cross-version extension strategy and mark the transform as not core-R4-equivalent. If preservation is not possible, reject the downgrade or flag it for manual review rather than silently omitting the filter. Tests should cover `valueFilter` with path-only, searchParam-only, comparator-present, and comparator-absent cases.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: The core addition is a reasonable way to improve expressivity in R6. A backward-compatible alternative would have been to standardize the filter as an extension first, making R4 and R6 artifacts able to carry the same content. The tradeoff is that extension semantics are less visible to generic consumers than a native element.
findings.reviewerNotesMd: Unlike R4/R6 `codeFilter` and `dateFilter`, the inspected R6 `valueFilter` does not show a local XOR invariant requiring exactly one of `path` or `searchParam`. Implementers may need profile or application-level checks to avoid ambiguous value filters.

freshReview.narrativeMd: R6 adds `DataRequirement.valueFilter` as an optional repeating element family; R4 has no corresponding core element. This does not make any R4-valid DataRequirement instance invalid in R6. The real issue is only reverse-direction: an R6 artifact that relies on value filters cannot be represented losslessly in R4 core, and an R4 parser receiving R6 content may reject or drop the unknown element. That is a down-conversion/interversion concern, not a reason to flag the R6 additive base design as a breaking R4-to-R6 problem.
keyEvidence: R4 StructureDefinition has no element id beginning DataRequirement.valueFilter.
R6 StructureDefinition defines DataRequirement.valueFilter as min 0, max *, type Element, isSummary true.
R6 valueFilter children include path, searchParam, comparator, and value[x]; value[x] allows dateTime, Period, and Duration.
R6 valueFilter.comparator is optional but required-bound, when present, to ValueSet/value-filter-comparator with eq, gt, lt, ge, le, sa, and eb.
freshReview.fmmEffect: The trial-use R4 status further lowers concern here because the finding is additive for R4-to-R6 validation. Even if DataRequirement is used in clinical knowledge artifacts, no existing R4 instance is invalidated by this new optional R6 capability.
freshReview.compatibilityMechanism: R6-to-R4 loss: R6 valueFilter content cannot be represented in R4 core and may be rejected or silently dropped by R4 tooling; there is no old-valid/new-invalid R4-to-R6 mechanism.
freshReview.lessBreakingAlternativeAssessment: No less-breaking R6 base design is needed to preserve R4 instances because they are already preserved. Standardizing only an extension or backporting an extension would help downgrade/round-trip workflows, but that is a mitigation and would make the R6-native constraint less discoverable and less consistently validated.
freshReview.comparisonToExisting: disagree with the existing high overall impact as an R4-to-R6 break. The existing report correctly identifies R6-to-R4 loss, but that should be treated as reverse-direction migration risk rather than a concerning base R6 addition.

findings.title: DataRequirement.subject[x] extensible binding changed to participant-resource-types

binding.description: The possible types of subjects for a data requirement (E.g., Patient, Practitioner, Organization, Location, etc.).

terminologyComparison.terminologyNotesMd: By code string, R6 keeps the R4 subject codes Patient, Practitioner, Organization, Location, and Device, and adds participant resource codes. The code system changes from R4 `resource-types` to R6 `fhir-types`.

oldState.narrativeMd: R4 allows `subjectCodeableConcept` or `subjectReference(Group)`. The CodeableConcept binding is extensible to `ValueSet/subject-type`, composed of selected `resource-types` codes.

binding.description: The possible types of subjects for a data requirement (E.g., Patient, Practitioner, Organization, Location, etc.).

terminologyComparison.terminologyNotesMd: R6 broadens the participant subject value set and uses the unified `fhir-types` system.

newState.narrativeMd: R6 preserves cardinality, choice types, the `Group` reference target, and `meaningWhenMissing = Patient`, but changes the CodeableConcept binding to `participant-resource-types`.

structuredDelta.matchingRationaleMd: The element id and path are unchanged, and the choice types are identical. The material difference is the extensible binding target and composed terminology system.

impact.impactRationaleMd: Because the binding is `extensible`, this is less hard than the `DataRequirement.type` required binding. However, terminology validators and conformance rules may flag R4 `resource-types` codings as not drawn from the R6 `participant-resource-types` ValueSet, and R6 participant subject codes such as `CareTeam` or `PractitionerRole` are outside the R4 subject-type value set. The JSON shape remains representable as CodeableConcept.
impact.safetyOrBusinessRiskMd: Incorrect subject interpretation can affect data scoping, but this change is primarily terminology/conformance risk rather than loss of structural data.

justification.inferredGoal: Broaden subject typing to participant resources and align terminology with R6 fhir-types.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Define the R6 participant-resource-types value set to accept the five legacy R4 resource-types subject codings alongside the canonical R6 fhir-types codes.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: The R6 goal of broadening subject choices and aligning with `fhir-types` is reasonable, but the compatibility cost from dropping the old `resource-types` codings appears avoidable. Because `subject[x]` uses `CodeableConcept` and an extensible binding, the base value set could have accepted legacy R4 codings while recommending canonical R6 codings. That would preserve most or all R4-valid subject instances with moderate terminology-normalization tradeoff, so the exclusive switch is probably avoidable.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: A less-breaking base design would compose `participant-resource-types` from the R6 `fhir-types` participant codes plus the R4 `resource-types` codes `Patient`, `Practitioner`, `Organization`, `Location`, and `Device` as legacy aliases or accepted codings. This is distinct from merely publishing a ConceptMap: base R6 validators would continue to accept old codings while producers migrate to `fhir-types`. The main cost is duplicated representations for the same subject concept and the risk that legacy codings persist indefinitely, but those costs seem moderate compared with rejecting or warning on common R4 codings.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: The tradeoff is dual terminology-system support and normalization burden, but it preserves R4 subject codings while still adding the broader R6 participant codes.

evidence.detail: R4 subject[x] is extensible-bound to ValueSet/subject-type.
R6 subject[x] is extensible-bound to ValueSet/participant-resource-types.
R4 uses resource-types codes Patient, Practitioner, Organization, Location, and Device. R6 uses fhir-types and adds CareTeam, Group, HealthcareService, PractitionerRole, and RelatedPerson.

examples.examplesMd: These are conformance-risk examples, not guaranteed hard structural failures. The first can be structurally parsed in R6 but may not satisfy the R6 extensible binding as cleanly as a `fhir-types` coding. The second is structurally parseable in R4 but is outside the R4 subject-type value set.

findings.narrativeMd: `subject[x]` retains the same choice shape, but the CodeableConcept terminology changes. The R6 binding is broader and arguably more consistent with participant resources, but systems that store or validate the coding system as well as the code must account for the shift from `resource-types` to `fhir-types`.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: This is not a clear hard instance break because the binding remains extensible and CodeableConcept can carry alternate codings. Still, strict terminology validation may produce warnings or errors depending on validator policy, and R6-only participant subject codes are not in the R4 value set. Runtime code that assumes the R4 five-code subject set may reject or mishandle new R6 subjects.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Normalize subject CodeableConcept codings to the R6 `http://hl7.org/fhir/fhir-types` system where possible while preserving original codings if round-trip fidelity matters. Add test cases for old R4 subject codings, new R6 participant subject codes, omitted subject with `Patient` meaningWhenMissing, and `subjectReference(Group)`, which remains unchanged.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: The change is probably justified because it covers more participant subject types and resolves the mismatch where R4 prose named subjects such as RelatedPerson that were absent from the R4 ValueSet. A backward-compatible design could have included both old and new systems or a formal ConceptMap, at the cost of more complex terminology normalization.
findings.reviewerNotesMd: A terminology expansion service would help confirm exact validator behavior for extensible bindings across systems.

freshReview.narrativeMd: `DataRequirement.subject[x]` keeps the same cardinality, choice types, `Reference(Group)` target, and `meaningWhenMissing = Patient`; the change is the extensible CodeableConcept binding. R4 binds selected subject resource types from the `resource-types` system, while R6 binds participant resources from the unified `fhir-types` system and adds subject codes such as `CareTeam`, `PractitionerRole`, and `RelatedPerson`. Because the binding remains extensible, this is not a hard structural break, but R4 codings like `http://hl7.org/fhir/resource-types|Patient` may no longer satisfy strict R6 terminology checks without adding a canonical `fhir-types` coding. Since subject scoping is explicitly described as critical and tied to CQL context, the avoidable warning/conformance churn is worth renewed design review.
keyEvidence: R4 StructureDefinition DataRequirement.subject[x]: min 0, max 1, types CodeableConcept or Reference(Group), extensible binding to http://hl7.org/fhir/ValueSet/subject-type, meaningWhenMissing Patient.

R6 StructureDefinition DataRequirement.subject[x]: same cardinality, choice types, Reference(Group) target, and meaningWhenMissing Patient, but extensible binding to http://hl7.org/fhir/ValueSet/participant-resource-types.

R4 ValueSet/subject-type includes resource-types codes Patient, Practitioner, Organization, Location, and Device; R6 ValueSet/participant-resource-types includes fhir-types codes CareTeam, Device, Group, HealthcareService, Location, Organization, Patient, Practitioner, PractitionerRole, and RelatedPerson.
The DataRequirement.subject[x] comment in both R4 and R6 says the subject is critical, limits data by relationship to the subject, and corresponds to the CQL context declaration.
freshReview.fmmEffect: Trial-use R4 status softens the stability concern and keeps this below a hard-break alarm. It does not eliminate concern because the path controls data scoping in knowledge artifacts and the compatibility-preserving terminology design appears modest.
freshReview.compatibilityMechanism: warning-level: the wire shape is unchanged, but the extensible binding and code system switch can create terminology validation warnings or warnings-as-errors for R4 resource-types codings; reverse conversion also loses the added R6 participant subject codes.
freshReview.lessBreakingAlternativeAssessment: A less-breaking R6 base design could compose participant-resource-types from the canonical R6 fhir-types participant codes plus the five legacy R4 resource-types subject codings as deprecated/accepted aliases. The tradeoff is dual terminology-system support and normalization burden, but CodeableConcept can carry multiple codings and the cost seems moderate compared with invalidating or warning on common R4 subject codings.
freshReview.comparisonToExisting: partially agree with the existing medium-impact assessment: it is not a hard structural break, but the warning-level conformance risk is real. I agree with the existing less-breaking-alternative direction and judge it strong enough to warrant Revisit.

checkedNoMaterialChange.notesMd: Canonical URL, id, name, kind, type, and abstract flag are stable. Status changed from draft/trial-use to active/normative, which is notable but not an instance-breaking identity change. The baseDefinition shift is out of scope as a base-hierarchy issue.
For pre-existing local elements, min/max cardinalities were unchanged. The only new cardinalities belong to the added optional R6 `valueFilter` element family, covered in a finding.

Pre-existing local element type lists were stable: `subject[x]` remains CodeableConcept or Reference, `dateFilter.value[x]` remains dateTime/Period/Duration, and primitive/string/code/canonical/positiveInt uses did not materially change.
`DataRequirement.subjectReference` remains targeted to `Group`; no local reference target was removed, added, or replaced.

Local invariants `drq-1` and `drq-2` retain the same error severity, human text, and FHIRPath expression `path.exists() xor searchParam.exists()`. R6 adds source/condition metadata, but that does not change the validation rule.
No local DataRequirement element became a modifier or stopped being a modifier.
Pre-existing local summary flags were unchanged. New R6 `valueFilter` elements are summary elements, but that is part of the additive element finding.
No local DataRequirement slicing changed. Extension slicing is inherited from Element/Extension and excluded.
No local fixed value, pattern, or default value was added, removed, or changed.
No local minValue, maxValue, maxLength, or regex constraint change was found.

Serialized names for pre-existing local elements and choice suffixes are stable. R6 adds new serialized names under `valueFilter`; that is covered as an R6-to-R4 representability finding rather than a serialization change to existing fields.

Most local definitions/comments are unchanged except spelling/capitalization updates such as `resolveable` to `resolvable` and `Valueset` to `ValueSet`. The added `valueFilter` semantics and terminology binding changes are handled as findings.

`sort.direction` remains required-bound to `ValueSet/sort-direction`; the version changes but the local code system still contains `ascending` and `descending` with unchanged definitions. Material binding changes for `type`, `subject[x]`, and new `valueFilter.comparator` are covered elsewhere.

nonBreakingNotableChanges.title: Standards status advanced from trial-use/draft to normative/active
nonBreakingNotableChanges.whyNotBreakingMd: Maturity and publication status changes do not by themselves invalidate instances or change the JSON/XML shape.
nonBreakingNotableChanges.migrationAwarenessMd: The normative/active status may affect governance expectations and implementer willingness to rely on the R6 shape. It also makes local breaking changes more important to handle deliberately.

nonBreakingNotableChanges.title: Local drq-1 and drq-2 invariants gained explicit source/condition metadata without expression changes
nonBreakingNotableChanges.whyNotBreakingMd: The FHIRPath expressions and human rule text remain the same, so validation behavior for the local rule is materially unchanged.
nonBreakingNotableChanges.migrationAwarenessMd: Tools that display constraint provenance may show the rules as sourced from `StructureDefinition/DataRequirement` in R6.

nonBreakingNotableChanges.title: sort.direction ValueSet version changed but code content is stable
nonBreakingNotableChanges.whyNotBreakingMd: Both local R4 and R6 sort-direction CodeSystems contain the same `ascending` and `descending` codes with unchanged definitions.
nonBreakingNotableChanges.migrationAwarenessMd: Regenerated terminology packages will point to the R6 ValueSet version, but existing sort direction values should continue to validate.

followUpDependencies.reasonMd: R6 DataRequirement specializes `DataType` rather than `Element`. Per assignment rules this base-hierarchy shift is out of scope here but may affect generated class hierarchies and inherited rules globally.

followUpDependencies.reasonMd: `DataRequirement.type` migration requires authoritative mappings for removed, renamed, split, or merged FHIR type/resource codes. The local package comparison identifies the gap but cannot safely infer every semantic mapping.
A terminology-server expansion and validator behavior check would improve confidence about `subject[x]` extensible binding migration and old `resource-types` codings.
